title: Anorexia nervosa among children and adolescents – a pilot study of standardized strength training as a complementary therapeutic approach in an inpatient setting
summary: The AnanS project is a feasibility study of an individualised and supervised machine-based strength training for young women with Anorexia nervosa in an inpatient setting. Before a randomised, controlled trial can be conducted to examine the effectiveness of strength training on the course of treatment, health and general motivation for therapy, this pilot study must first assess key aspects relating to its implementation. The study will include female patients aged between 12 and 18 who have been diagnosed with Anorexia nervosa and are being treated in an inpatient setting. As an additional therapeutic component for the treatment of Anorexia nervosa, the individualized and supervised strength training will be carried out over 12 weeks (3x/week), preceded by a two-week adaptation phase with strength training machines.

interventions.name: Machine-based strength training – total duration of 14 weeks, comprising two-week adaptation phase (strength endurance training 3x/week) followed by 12-week training phase (strength training 3X/week).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
In-patient female patients aged between 12 and 18 with a diagnosis of Anorexia nervosa; a dietary plan in place; agreement with the treatment plan and willingness to undertake training under supervision; general ability to cope with the demands of daily life (able to participate in all in-patient treatment programmes)
Exclusion criteria:
Persistent bradycardia or symptomatic bradycardia, particularly in cases of syncope; abnormal ECG findings, particularly high-degree arrhythmias; marked orthostatic dysregulation with a significant drop in systolic blood pressure and clinically significant hypotension; Clinically significant electrolyte disturbances; marked renal or hepatic dysfunction, including pathological elevations in creatinine, urea or transaminases; severe acute infections; severe to moderate anaemia; orthopaedic contraindications to physical exertion (e.g. pain, fractures, tendinopathies); Hypothermia; severe dyspnoea at rest or even with minimal exertion; chest pain, dizziness or palpitations; indications in the psychopathological assessment that attention, impulse control or safety in the training setting are significantly impaired; acute suicidal ideation
